title: opaque-slice-orchestrator-with-rollback-windowing-and-telemetry-safepoints
author: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation: teams need fine-grained, privacy-preserving cohorting for multi-arm experiments and phased promotes without leaking slice identities across services. This PR introduces the 'Opaque Slice Orchestrator'—a rollout layer that assigns opaque slice tokens to user cohorts, schedules time-windowed promotes, and enforces rollback windows driven by telemetry safepoints. Key goals: (1) session-consistent routing for promoted clients, (2) rollback windowing so automatic reversions respect a minimum quarantine period before re-promote, (3) telemetry-driven safepoints so automated rollback triggers are only evaluated at stable aggregation boundaries, and (4) A/B pairing support for paired metric diffs and counterfactual capture.

What this PR does: implements a new orchestrator component in the rollout controller, adds a lightweight tokenization layer to generate opaque slice IDs (no user PII retained), extends the rollout API to accept 'sliceAffinity' and 'rollbackWindow' parameters, instruments telemetry hooks for safepoint flushes, and adds a controller-level simulation harness to validate failure-mode behavior. The description below is a continuous narrative that includes checklist, test surface, and merge notes.

Checklist: - [x] design doc (ENG-4829) linked - [x] unit + integration tests for token lifecycle - [x] e2e staged deployment in canary cluster - [x] migration path for existing cohort rules - [x] docs and API changelog - [x] security review (no user id persistence)

Behavioral highlights: - Opaque slice tokens are stable per-cohort across 72h by default (configurable) but rotate on manual remap to avoid long-lived correlations. - RollbackWindow: a minimum time an experiment must remain in quarantine before attempting automatic re-promotion; prevents churn loops on noisy metrics. - Telemetry safepoints: the orchestrator evaluates metric gates only after configured aggregation windows (e.g., 5m/1h buckets) to avoid acting on transient spikes. - A/B pairing: when enabled the router maintains paired user-to-variant mapping to ensure within-subject comparisons for metrics like CTR and latency.

Compatibility and migration: - Backwards compatible with existing cohort rules: if 'sliceAffinity' absent, behaviour is unchanged. - Admins can opt-in per-rollout via the console or API. - The feature flags allow gradual ramp of tokenization and safepoint enforcement.

Commit summary: see commits field for short messages. Files changed: rollout controller, router shard, telemetry aggregator hooks, API contract, migration script, and test harness. Small illustrative snippet added in rollout_controller.go to show time-window guard:

if now.Sub(rollout.LastQuarantineStart) < rollout.RollbackWindow {
    // hold promotion until window expires
    return ErrQuarantineWindow
}

Tests and CI: initial CI run showed a flaky aggregator test; test fixed by introducing time-simulated aggregator in tests and adding deterministic clocks to the harness. Final CI run: pass. Load test: canary cluster exercises 20k concurrent sessions with <=5% overhead on routing compared to baseline.

Operational playbook (short): - Default rollout in beta cluster for 48h. - Monitor 'orchestrator.slice_rotate' and 'orchestrator.rollback_evaluations' metrics. - If rollback oscillation observed, increase RollbackWindow and widen telemetry aggregation window. - Emergency stop available via console -> rollouts -> abort and snapshot.

Related work: builds on ENG-3911 (traffic fencing) and ENG-4522 (session affinity), pairs with SUP-1304 support runbook for incident rollback. This PR is intended to reduce false-positive automated rollbacks and enable privacy-safe paired A/B experiments.

Merge notes: squash merge; migration script will be run as a background job during the next maintenance window. No DB schema breaking changes.
